Name: Run-to-failure vibration dataset of a three-stages planetary gearbox
Summary: Hourly radial vibration recordings from a three-stage planetary gearbox run on a back-to-back bench until its sun gear failed after 1006 hours.
Description:
The Department of Engineering at the University of Ferrara recorded this run-to-failure history of a three-stage planetary gearbox. The test bench couples two identical electric motor and planetary gearbox assemblies back to back: the driving side runs in speed-control mode and the opposite side in torque-control mode to impose the load.

Five operating conditions, combinations of rotational speed and resistant torque, were applied cyclically for one hour each. Every hour, a PCB 352A60 mono-axial accelerometer on the gearbox housing recorded radial vibration for 5 minutes at 20 kHz through an NI cRIO controller with a 9234 analog module. The test ran until the third-stage sun gear failed completely after 1006 operating hours.

Data is provided as .mat files, each holding the radial acceleration signal, the sampling frequency and the operating condition of one acquisition. The record is split into three parts of about one third of the experiment each and serves diagnostics, prognostics and remaining useful life prediction.
